name: Open Origins
kicker: Open Origins · open research, started November 2026
goal: Map and test every route to the origin of life, by 2027
lede: Chemists have shown many single steps from simple molecules toward life. Nobody has joined them into one continuous route. We score each proposed route step by step, re-test published claims against chance, and seal predictions that future data can confirm.
odds: The open goal: scored map, 10 claims benched, 3 predictions confirmed
raise_odds: New Bennu or Ryugu compound tables released after we seal predictions about them.
A lab reporting sustained exponential replication by a small ribozyme, which we model before the result is out.
One wet lab agreeing to run a test we pre-register.
criteria_intro: Two questions, kept apart: can chemistry do it at all, and what actually happened on Earth? "Cracked" means one stated setting and one route from its raw materials to a system that copies itself with heritable variation, where:
criteria: **Every step has a published yield** from a lab other than us.
**Every step follows from the last** by a named physical process, under a compatibility rule we hash in advance, with no purified hand-offs.
**The route predicts new data:** a kinetic model fitted on the earlier steps predicts at least 3 measurements published after the hash.
**It survives a red team** that did not build it.
ladder_intro: From building blocks to evolution. A separate track asks what happened on Earth (LUCA, timing, setting).
ladder: Made from a stated setting. Bennu's returned sample holds 33 amino acids, all five nucleobases and ribose.
Joined into chains under compatible conditions, without purifying between steps.
A molecule copies function-length sequences. The 45-nucleotide QT45 ribozyme copied itself and its complement (Science 2026), under engineered conditions.
Exponential growth from the setting's own feedstocks.
not_claimed: **That a working route is what happened.** Showing a route is possible is not showing it is the one Earth took.
**Wet-lab results of our own.** We compute and reanalyse; only labs and sample-return missions can confirm.
**Any citation we have not checked.** Every reference passes a DOI audit before it appears here.
theories_lede: Each origin-of-life theory, the prediction it can least afford to get wrong, and the evidence from 2023-2026.

theories.name: RNA world
theories.prediction: Small polymerase ribozymes are common in sequence space and can run a closed copying cycle.
theories.evidence: For: QT45 (Gianni, Holliger et al., Science 2026) copies itself from triplet building blocks in alkaline ice. Against: the building blocks are pre-activated and supplied by the experimenters; there is no exponential growth yet.

theories.name: Alkaline vents / metabolism first
theories.prediction: Natural pH gradients across iron-sulfur barriers drive CO2 reduction well past formate.
theories.evidence: Formate depends on the gradient (Hudson et al., PNAS 2020); micromolar formic and acetic acid reported (Altair et al., JACS 2025). Nothing beyond two-carbon products yet.

theories.name: Warm ponds / wet-dry cycling
theories.prediction: Repeated drying makes long, copyable polymers faster than water breaks them.
theories.evidence: Not yet reviewed; first item in our research sweep.

theories.name: Cyanosulfidic chemistry
theories.prediction: One UV-lit surface setting supplies nucleotide, amino acid and lipid precursors without incompatible steps.
theories.evidence: Strong step by step; needs reagents delivered in a set order, which strains continuity.

theories.name: Peptide-RNA co-evolution
theories.prediction: Amino acids attach to RNA in a selective way without enzymes, a first step toward coding.
theories.evidence: Thioester-driven aminoacylation of RNA near neutral pH (Singh, Powner et al., Nature 2025). Coding itself is unexplained.

theories.name: Autocatalytic sets (RAF)
theories.prediction: Self-sustaining reaction sets in real metabolism are more than an artefact of network size.
theories.evidence: A maxRAF of 1,335 reactions in an ancient anaerobic network (Xavier et al., 2020). Never tested against randomised networks.

theories.name: Assembly theory
theories.prediction: Molecules with assembly index above about 15, in many copies, occur only with life.
theories.evidence: Minerals score above 15 (Hazen et al., J R Soc Interface 2024); assembly index argued to be a compression measure (Uthamacumaran et al., 2024). Proponents dispute both.

theories.name: Homochirality
theories.prediction: A physical process biases one handedness strongly enough to be amplified.
theories.evidence: Bennu's amino acids are racemic, like Ryugu's, which counts against delivery from space. A magnetite spin route (Ozturk et al., 2023) gives about 35% excess after recrystallisation.

bench: does the real maxRAF fall outside what degree-preserving random networks and random food sets give?
does it beat molecular weight and atom count at separating biotic from abiotic samples?
LUCA as an anaerobic acetogen (Moody et al. 2024)
how much of the gene set survives changes to cutoffs, taxon sampling and the gene-transfer model?
does the claim survive the selection bias of the starting library?
scored step by step for compatible conditions, not by counting products made.
reported excess against contamination indicators, with Bennu and Ryugu as clean controls.
approach_lede: The same rules as our Indus script project, plus one more: every citation is checked, because AI agents invent references.
rules: Predictions, tests and pass marks are SHA-256 hashed before any result is seen. So is the rule for what makes two steps compatible.
Use nulls that respect the data.
Random networks keep each molecule's number of reactions; size-matched controls for assembly index; shuffled gene patterns for LUCA.
A method must find a planted autocatalytic core, a planted ancestor or a planted incompatible step before its real output counts.
Let someone else try to break it.
Every positive result goes to a red team that did not produce it.
Failed routes are written up with the size of effect the test could have caught.
traps: Several routes may all work; that does not say which one happened.
So we fix the rule in advance.
Most published steps start from purified chemicals; we mark every one.
A network that contains an autocatalytic set may never run.
Metabolic networks are biased toward today's enzymes; our nulls account for it.

map.title: Pathway map
map.lede: The route from geochemistry to evolving life, one step per row. A step counts as shown only if it works under conditions the previous step could provide.
steps: Feedstocks (HCN, formaldehyde, phosphate, sulfides) in a stated setting
Several settings proposed; each supplies a different subset.
Made in many routes; found in Bennu and Ryugu samples (2025).
Ribose found in Bennu (Furukawa et al. 2025); nucleotide routes need ordered steps (Sutherland).
Thioester routes near neutral pH (Singh et al. 2025).
Shown with purified inputs; continuity unscored.
QT45 copies itself and its complement in ice (2026).
Compartments that grow and divide with their contents
RNA-catalysed evolution of a catalytic RNA (Papastavrou, Horning & Joyce, PNAS 2024), not open-ended.
map.note: These statuses come from the literature. Our own scoring, under a compatibility rule hashed in advance, replaces them as the step tables land (tracker tasks #3-#5).

scenarios.name: Alkaline hydrothermal vents
scenarios.explains: a natural energy source (pH gradients) and CO2 reduction to formate and acetate.

scenarios.name: Cyanosulfidic surface chemistry
scenarios.explains: common origins for nucleotide, amino acid and lipid precursors under UV light.
scenarios.gap: needs reagents delivered in a set order.

scenarios.name: Ice (eutectic freezing)
scenarios.explains: concentrates RNA and slows breakdown; QT45 works here.
scenarios.gap: where the activated triplets come from.

contribute: **Rerun a test.** Every result has code and a sealed pre-registration in the repository.
**Attack a result.** Red-team tasks are open on the tracker.
**Fix a step.** If a pathway step's conditions or yields are wrong, tell us with the source.
**Run a sealed test in your lab.** Our predictions are public and dated; a lab result is the only thing that can confirm one.
